chunks: Whoever can at that time keep himself clinging to Allah, let him do so. If you follow me, then I shall carry you, if Allah wills, upon the path of Paradise, even though it may be full of severe hardship and bitter taste.
ai.seo_question: What is the promise of Paradise in exchange for enduring hardship according to Nahj al-Balagha?
ai.summary: Delivered during the Battle of the Camel, this passage underscores Imam Ali’s (AS) call for steadfastness (thabat) amidst the political and military turmoil of Basra, framing obedience to him as a divine pathway to salvation. The mention of 'severe hardship' (mashaqqah) reflects the Shia scholarly view that true adherence to the Imam often entails enduring significant trials, aligning with the concept of 'sabr' (patience) in the face of adversity.
